name: Cefixime
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: About 50% of absorbed cefixime is excreted unchanged in urine, and its half-life rises from 3 to 4 hours to about 11.5 hours in severe kidney impairment. The US label keeps the usual 400 mg daily dose at creatinine clearance (CrCl) 60 mL/min or more and gives reduced daily volumes of the oral suspension below that, with the same reduced doses on hemodialysis and CAPD. Dialysis does not remove significant amounts.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses CrCl (mL/min); bands at 60 and 20. Reduced doses are given as suspension volumes.

bands.recommendation: CrCl 60 or more: usual dose (400 mg daily) (label).
CrCl 21–59: 13 mL/day of the 100 mg/5 mL suspension or 6.5 mL/day of the 200 mg/5 mL suspension (about 260 mg/day) (label Table 2; mg values calculated from the label volumes).

CrCl 21–29: 13 mL/day of the 100 mg/5 mL suspension or 6.5 mL/day of the 200 mg/5 mL suspension (about 260 mg/day). CrCl 20 or less: 8.6 mL/day of the 100 mg/5 mL suspension or 4.4 mL/day of the 200 mg/5 mL suspension (about 172 to 176 mg/day) (label Table 2; mg values calculated).
CrCl 20 or less: 8.6 mL/day of the 100 mg/5 mL suspension or 4.4 mL/day of the 200 mg/5 mL suspension (about 172 to 176 mg/day) (label Table 2; mg values calculated).

hd: Same as CrCl 21–59: 13 mL/day of the 100 mg/5 mL suspension or 6.5 mL/day of the 200 mg/5 mL suspension (about 260 mg/day) (label Table 2). Not removed significantly by hemodialysis; no supplement. Monitor carefully (label).
pd: Continuous peritoneal dialysis: same as CrCl 20 or less: 8.6 mL/day of the 100 mg/5 mL suspension or 4.4 mL/day of the 200 mg/5 mL suspension (about 172 to 176 mg/day) (label Table 2). Not removed significantly by peritoneal dialysis.
crrt: Not in label; the cited CRRT review (Li 2020) gives no regimen for this drug. Specialist input.
dialyzable: No: neither hemodialysis nor peritoneal dialysis removes significant amounts (label). About 65% protein bound.
monitoring: CrCl for dose; patients on dialysis should be monitored carefully (label 5.3); prothrombin time with warfarin or in patients at risk; diarrhea (CDAD).

pediatric.usual_dose: 8 mg/kg/day of the suspension, once daily or as 4 mg/kg every 12 hours (label).
pediatric.max_dose: Children over 45 kg or older than 12 years: adult dose (label).

renal.recommendation: No pediatric kidney dosing in label (the reduced-dose table is for adults). Specialist input.
